title: Ephemeral-cast routing + attention tiling for mixed-precision INT8/FP8 serving paths
creator: Mei Lawson
description: Goal: reduce measurable dequant/cast overhead when routing requests between INT8 and FP8 execution paths by introducing ephemeral-cast kernels and an attention-tiling strategy that minimizes intermediate memory copies and kernel launches during prefill and decode. This ticket covers design, prototype kernels, planner changes, microbenchmarks, and fallbacks for correctness and numeric parity checks.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end median token latency improvement >= 8% for typical chat workloads vs current INT8/FP8 mixed baseline
Dequant-related overhead (measured as time spent in host-device copies + cast kernels) reduced by >= 30% in microbenchmarks
Numeric divergence vs FP16 baseline within configured tolerance (L2 distance <= 0.002 on evaluation prompt set)
No regression in throughput targets for dedicated pools; automated smoke tests in CI that run new kernels on one CUDA machine
Feature gate + runtime flag implemented so rollout can be A/Bed per-customer and rolled back without model changes
implementation_notes: Introduce ephemeral-cast kernels that perform on-GPU bitwidth cast inside fused attention / matmul epilogues to avoid persistent dequant buffers
Add an attention-tiling option in the kernel API that prefers tiled QKV dispatch to keep KV cache layout contiguous for decode and prefill; enables single-kernel prefill for common sequence shapes
Extend kernel selector with a new score: cast_penalty_estimate which penalizes plans requiring a host/device cast or extra kernel launch

Planner change: prefer INT8/FP8 fused kernels when cast_penalty_estimate + latency_model predicts lower end-to-end cost; otherwise fall back to FP16 path. Add explicit compatibility matrix mapping model ops to ephemeral-cast variants
Microbench harness: create per-layer microbench scripts (bench_ephemeral_cast.py) to measure latency, memory, and L2 error across seq-len distributions (prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, mixed)
Provide a Software-flag gate (REDWOOD_EPHEMERAL_CAST=on) and API toggle to enable for internal canaries; default off for 2.4 GA until full numeric tests are run
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created by Mei. Initial design sketch posted to Confluence (see links).

2026-03-11: Spike: implemented prototype ephemeral-cast epilogue on local devbox (A100). Observed ~26% reduction in dequant kernel time on microbench for 1x batch, seq512. Baseline comparison against existing INT8 path. — Ravi

2026-03-12: Design review with research and runtime teams. Key feedback: ensure attention-tiling does not worsen KV cache fragmentation for long-running decode streams; add regression test for canary workloads. Agreed to add a contiguous-KV layout option alongside tiling.

2026-03-12: PR opened for prototype kernels: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1289 — includes kernel, unit tests, and bench harness. Marked WIP due to failing numeric tolerance on 2 of 50 eval prompts.

2026-03-13: Investigating numeric drift: found one cast-order edge case in layernorm+qkv fused path. Patch prepared to reorder casts inside epilogue; expect fixes to bring L2 distance within acceptance. Also starting on planner scoring change RFC.
notes_for_reviewers: When reviewing PR 1289 focus on the epilogue reorder changes — they affect numeric parity and perf trade-offs
Benchmarks in the PR use synthetic prompts; please run the bench harness against the replicated internal eval set under /benchdata/quant_eval to validate
There is a runtime flag gating planner changes; ensure that default behaviour remains identical when flag is off
